# From Chat Box to Assistant {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

So far you *talked* to AI. Now you put it to work.

## Why Cowork? {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="why" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em;"}
**Claude Cowork** is the fastest way to turn AI into an assistant that works on your
**actual files** — not just a chat tab.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## Portable idea
Other tools have their own version of this. We use Cowork because the setup is the
simplest — the concepts move with you.
:::

## Chat vs. Assistant {auto-animate=true}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment .fade-in}

# Setup {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

A few clicks — hands on

## Three Steps to Running {auto-animate=true}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Install** the Claude desktop app and sign in
2. **Open Cowork** and point it at a **folder** on your computer
3. **Type a task** in plain language — and approve what it proposes
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
That's it. No setup files, no code, no configuration.
:::

## Meet the Working Directory {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="dir" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
When Cowork opens, it points at one **folder on your computer** — its **working directory.**
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em; margin-top: 1em;"}
*"So **that's** the office the two layers talked about."*
:::

. . .

This folder **is** the office. Your context lives here as real, openable files.

## What Cowork Can Do {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
| Feature | In plain language |
|---|---|
| **Read / edit / create files** | Works on your real documents |
| **Skills** | Saved recipe cards it can reuse *(next)* |
| **`/schedule`** | A standing appointment to run a task *(next)* |
| **Plugins** | Bundles of skills + connections for a role |
| **Dispatch** | Clicks around apps when there's no shortcut |
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #00C9A7; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
Today we focus on files, Skills, and Schedule.
:::

# Agent-Era Safety {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

The second rule

## One Rule Was Enough — Until Now {auto-animate=true}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #1C355E;"}
**Rule 1 — Newspaper Test**

Guards what you *paste **in***.

*(sanitize student data first)*
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
**Rule 2 — The Undo Test**

Guards what the agent ***does***.

*(industry term: blast radius)*
:::
:::
:::
::::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
An agent that can *act* needs a second rule.
:::

## The Undo Test & Human-in-the-Loop {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="blast" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.05em;"}
Before letting it act, ask:
*"What's the worst it could do if it's wrong — can I undo it, and who'd notice in time?"*
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #666; font-size: 0.85em;"}
*(industry term: **blast radius**)*
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-important}
## Always start in draft / notify-me mode
Cowork **proposes, you approve**. Promote to **act-on-its-own** only after it has proven
itself.
:::

## Our Workshop Rule {auto-animate=true}

::: {style="background: #00C9A7; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.5em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.2em;"}
All hands-on work runs in a **sandbox folder** with **dummy data**.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
A mistake can't touch a real grade sheet or a real inbox while you're learning.
:::

## Micro-Check — Act Now or Propose & Wait? {auto-animate=true}

**1.** "Reformat these notes into a clean summary in a new file."

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #00C9A7; color: white; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center;"}
**Act now** — low blast radius, easy to undo.
:::
:::

. . .

**2.** "Email the revised grades to all 60 students."

. . .

::: {.fragment .fade-in}
::: {style="background: #FF7A5C; color: white; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center;"}
**Propose & wait** — irreversible, high blast radius. Review first.
:::
:::

# Skills {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #FF7A5C)"}

A saved recipe card

## What a Skill Is {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="anatomy" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #FF7A5C;"}
A **recipe card filed in the office.** You say "make the weekly digest" and Cowork pulls
the card and follows it — you don't re-explain the steps.
:::

. . .

A Skill is just three things:

::: {.incremental}
- **A name** — what you call it
- **When to use it (the trigger)** — the phrase that makes it reach for the card
- **The steps** — the recipe, in plain language *(that's a "script")*
:::

## Demo 1 — "Build-a-Deck" {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="deck" style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; text-align: center; font-size: 1.1em;"}
Lecture notes → an on-brand slide deck you can export to **`.pptx`**
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.78em; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
**Name:** Build-a-Deck &nbsp;•&nbsp; **Trigger:** *"turn these notes into a lecture deck"*

**Steps:** 1) outline the storyline · 2) one idea per slide · 3) apply my course style ·
4) export a **`.pptx`**
:::

## Invoke It on Fresh Input {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="deck" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7; font-size: 0.85em;"}
Skill saved — now just **type the trigger** on any new lecture:
:::

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 0.8em; border-radius: 12px; font-style: italic; font-size: 0.85em; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
"Turn this into a **lecture deck**: photosynthesis — light reactions, Calvin cycle,
limiting factors, today's lab."
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #00C9A7; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
One phrase → a downloadable deck. No re-explaining.
:::

# Scripts {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #9B8EC0)"}

When the task is *calculation*

## A Script Is a Recipe Card {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="script" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
A **recipe card** of steps, written down once, so a job runs the same way every time —
whether a person or the agent follows it.
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
## Not a programmer thing
A "script" is just *"do these steps, in this order, every time."* **You never write code**
in this workshop — you describe the steps in plain language…
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
…and Cowork **writes and runs the script for you.**
:::

## Demo 2 — Grade Summaries {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="calc" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #9B8EC0;"}
You have a spreadsheet of raw scores. You want weighted finals, the class average, and a
distribution — every term.
:::

. . .

::: {style="background: #1C355E; color: #ffffff; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-style: italic; font-size: 0.85em; text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em;"}
"From `grades.csv`, compute each student's weighted total (midterm 30%, final 40%,
project 30%), the class average, and a grade distribution. Save it as a new sheet."
:::

## Why a Script Here {auto-animate=true}

::: {.incremental}
- Cowork **writes a small script** to do the math — exactly, every row, every time
- It runs the same way next term — no formula errors, no copy-paste
- You never see code unless you ask — you get the **result**
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pair it with "double-check"
For anything graded, ask it to compute **twice and compare** before you trust the numbers.
:::

# Schedule {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

A standing appointment

## A Standing Appointment {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="cron" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1.2em; border-radius: 12px; border-left: 4px solid #00C9A7;"}
Type **`/schedule`** in any Cowork task. *"Every Sunday at 5pm, draft my week-ahead
teaching summary."* It just happens — you didn't have to ask.
:::

. . .

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.5em;"}
The leap from *a tool you operate* to *a teammate that acts on its own.*
:::

## Demo 3 — Weekly Digest (Notify-Me) {auto-animate=true}

::: {data-id="digest" style="background: #f7f9fc; padding: 1em; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.85em;"}
**`/schedule`:** Every Sunday 5pm — scan the course folder and **draft** a summary of
what's due, ungraded, and upcoming. **Notify me; don't send anything.**
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-important}
## Guardrails first
Every scheduled job starts in **draft / notify-me** mode. Promote to act-on-its-own only
after you've watched it get it right.
:::

## Key Takeaways {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Cowork ≠ chat** — it opens files, runs steps, and can act
2. **Setup is three clicks** — install, point at a folder, type a task; the working directory **is** the office
3. **Second safety rule** — the undo test / human-in-the-loop (*blast radius*); sandbox + dummy data
4. **Skill** — a saved recipe you invoke by a trigger; **Script** — Cowork writes the steps to crunch data exactly
5. **Schedule (`/schedule`)** — a standing appointment; guardrails first: every job starts in draft / notify-me
:::
